# Distribution Matrix Audit — v2.4.0-rc3

**Verdict: 🔴 NO-GO — Release promotion blocked (3 blockers, 1 global/critical)**

## Status Table

| Region | Artifact | SHA256 | Object Storage | Container Registry | Regional Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AWS us-east-1 | tar.gz | `e3b0c442…b855` | S3: 200 OK (Verified) | ECR: `v2.4.0-rc3` (Verified) | 🔴 FAIL — hash anomaly |
| AWS us-gov-west-1 | tar.gz | `e3b0c442…b855` | S3: **403 SignatureDoesNotMatch** (presign expired) | ECR: **MISSING** | 🔴 FAIL — distribution incomplete |
| GCP us-central1 | tar.gz | `e3b0c442…b855` | GCS: 200 OK (Verified) | Artifact Registry: `v2.4.0-rc3` (Verified) | 🔴 FAIL — hash anomaly |

## Blockers

**B1 — CRITICAL (global): All artifacts hash to the empty-input digest.**
`e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` is the well-known SHA256 of a **zero-byte input**. All three regions report this exact hash, which means one of two things — both release-blocking:
- The published tarballs are **empty files** (build produced no content), or
- The hash-computation step in the pipeline is broken (hashing an empty stream/variable).

The "Verified / 200 OK" results in us-east-1 and us-central1 confirm only **HTTP reachability, not content integrity**. No region currently has a verifiably non-empty artifact. Because the identical hash appears across all regions, the root cause is almost certainly **upstream at build time**, not per-region replication.

**B2 — HIGH (us-gov-west-1): S3 artifact unretrievable.**
